discovered.description: Palette roles, restraint, semantic consistency, and when fewer colors means better design. Use when building color palettes, evaluating color usage, or diagnosing color-related design problems.

discovered.name: constraint-evaluation
discovered.description: Understand the constraints a design was built under and evaluate quality within that context. Use when reviewing work that had limited time, budget, or team size, or when assessing whether constraints were handled well.

discovered.name: consumption-discipline
discovered.description: Structured exposure habits for building taste through relentless, intentional consumption. Not passive scrolling. Active intake across design, architecture, film, music, food, and culture. Use when building a taste practice, advising on professional development, or diagnosing why someone's design range feels narrow.

discovered.name: craft-signals
discovered.description: Consistent radii, pixel-perfect alignment, state coverage, and the details that signal design quality. Use when polishing designs, auditing quality, or evaluating whether a design is ready to ship.

discovered.name: critique-vocabulary
discovered.description: Precise language for design feedback. Ban vague words. Name what you actually see. Use when giving design feedback, running critiques, or training teams to communicate about quality.

discovered.name: cross-domain-seeing
discovered.description: Pull design principles from architecture, fashion, film, industrial design, and physical spaces into screen-based design. Use when seeking inspiration beyond digital, expanding creative range, or building cross-disciplinary design vocabulary.

discovered.name: cross-pollination
discovered.description: Draw from architecture, fashion, music, food, and industrial design to expand your design taste range. Use when seeking inspiration beyond digital, building diverse reference sets, or expanding creative vocabulary.

discovered.name: daily-routines
discovered.description: 15-minute daily taste exercises. Monday through Friday. Compound effect over time. Use when building personal practice habits, training a team's design eye, or adding structure to professional development.

discovered.name: decision-tracing
discovered.description: Reverse-engineer why a design decision was made. Move from observation to inference. Use when studying products you admire, learning from competitors, or building analytical design thinking.

discovered.name: design-critique
discovered.description: Run taste-informed design reviews using Observation > Principle > Question. Use when facilitating design critiques, improving feedback quality on a team, or building a shared vocabulary for quality.

discovered.name: design-ranking
discovered.description: Rank multiple design solutions and explain why. Separate personal preference from quality judgment. Use when comparing design options, evaluating competing approaches, or making design decisions with clear reasoning.

discovered.name: design-rationale
discovered.description: Defend a design decision to skeptical stakeholders with structure and evidence. Use when presenting design work, writing design documentation, or pushing back on requests to change something.

discovered.name: detail-observation
discovered.description: Micro-decision analysis. Catalog the border radii, spacing scales, type sizes, and state coverage that most people miss. Use when auditing design systems, evaluating craft quality, or training granular perception.

discovered.name: dg-piagent
discovered.description:
Use when working with pi-agent / @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent SDK — 创建 agent、自定义工具、
编写扩展、修改系统提示词、管理会话、配置模型、处理认证、加载 skills/prompts/context files、
实现完全控制模式、或任何需要调用 pi-agent SDK API 的任务时使用。
也用于企业内网接口接入评估：用户给出企业/内网 LLM 接口文档或地址，问「能不能接」「怎么配」时，
按接口核对清单给出接入建议 + models.json 配置初稿。
触发关键词：createAgentSession、AgentSession、pi.on、session.subscribe、extensionFactories、
ModelRegistry、defineTool、pi-coding-agent、pi-ai、@earendil-works、SSE 流式集成、
企业接口文档、内网模型接入、OpenAI 兼容判断、接口接入评估。

discovered.name: field-notes
discovered.description: Structured taste breakdowns of real products. The format for making taste observations legible and shareable. Use when analyzing products, writing case studies, documenting design observations, or teaching through example.

discovered.name: flow-patterns
discovered.description: Task sequences, progressive disclosure, and the pacing of an experience over time. Use when designing multi-step flows, evaluating onboarding, or diagnosing why users get lost.

discovered.name: hierarchy-principles
discovered.description: Visual weight, attention order, and the decisions that guide the eye. Use when building layouts, evaluating information architecture, or diagnosing why a design feels confusing.

discovered.name: learning-by-making
discovered.description: Build taste through volume of output, deliberate failure, and speed. Taste cannot be developed by watching. It's sharpened by making, failing, and making again. Use when designing practice routines, breaking through creative blocks, or helping someone move from analysis to execution.

discovered.name: library-architecture
discovered.description: Build a reference system that returns the right reference in under 60 seconds. Use when setting up a design reference library, reorganizing existing collections, or helping teams build shared reference systems.

discovered.name: motion-design
discovered.description: Animation as communication. Feedback, orientation, emphasis, delight. If motion doesn't serve one of these four purposes, it shouldn't exist. Use when evaluating animation quality, designing transitions, or deciding whether motion adds or subtracts.

discovered.name: principle-tagging
discovered.description: Tag design references by principle, not aesthetic. Build a library you can actually search. Use when saving references, organizing inspiration, or building a design library that returns useful results.

discovered.name: python-anti-patterns
discovered.description: Diagnose and review Python problems in exception handling, repeated infrastructure logic, resource lifetime, async blocking, input and type contracts, or harmful coupling. Use during debugging, review, legacy maintenance, or implementation when concrete risks appear. Judge behavior and maintenance cost before changing code; skip unrelated or mechanical edits and harmless intentional duplication.

discovered.name: python-design-patterns
discovered.description: Guide Python feature design, implementation, and refactoring when responsibilities, coupling, module boundaries, testability, or extensibility require structural judgment. Use for tangled services, entangled I/O, or meaningful abstraction choices, including problems discovered during work. Choose the simplest maintainable design supported by the project; skip mechanical edits with no design decision.

discovered.name: quality-checklist
discovered.description: Systematic design quality evaluation. Hierarchy, type, color, space, craft, system. Use when evaluating whether a design is ready to ship, running quality audits, or setting quality standards.

discovered.name: screenshot-surgery
discovered.description: Annotate and map the anatomy of any design. Identify visual hierarchy, spacing systems, color roles, and tension points through clinical analysis. Use when doing formal design audits, teaching design analysis, or building structured observation skills.

discovered.name: search-first
discovered.description: Discover reusable repository code, dependencies, libraries, and extension points when adding or changing features, integrations, shared components, or utilities. Use when reuse could affect an implementation choice, including implicit needs discovered during work. Start with the project; research externally only to resolve a concrete gap. Skip prose and mechanical edits without such choices.

discovered.name: self-assessment
discovered.description: Diagnose your taste gaps across six skill areas. Know what to practice. Use when starting a taste development program, checking progress, or identifying specific areas to improve.

discovered.name: spatial-rhythm
discovered.description: Density, whitespace, rhythm, and how space communicates relationships between elements. Use when building layouts, evaluating spacing consistency, or diagnosing why a design feels cramped or empty.

discovered.name: system-deconstruction
discovered.description: Break a design system into its constituent decisions and evaluate each one. Use when auditing design systems, evaluating consistency, or understanding how a product maintains quality at scale.

discovered.name: taste-as-strategy
discovered.description: Use taste as a competitive moat and business advantage. In the AI and vibe-coding era, execution is commoditized. Taste is the defensible edge. Use when advising founders on product differentiation, building product culture, evaluating why some products win despite fewer features, or understanding taste as a strategic asset.

discovered.name: taste-gap
discovered.description: Navigate the gap between what you can see and what you can make. The Ira Glass gap. Use when a designer is frustrated by the distance between their taste and their output, when mentoring someone through a creative plateau, or when someone is considering quitting because their work doesn't match their vision.

discovered.name: taste-vs-trends
discovered.description: Tell the difference between design decisions that age well and decisions that follow the crowd. Use when evaluating whether a design choice is principled or fashionable, or when a client asks to 'make it look modern.'

discovered.name: teaching-taste
discovered.description: Help other designers develop judgment without imposing your style. Use when mentoring designers, running design education, or building team-wide quality standards.

discovered.name: timing-feedback
discovered.description: Response timing, acknowledgment, and making the interface feel alive. Every action deserves a response at the right speed. Use when designing interactions, evaluating responsiveness, or diagnosing why a product feels sluggish or dead.

discovered.name: tradeoff-assessment
discovered.description: Name what was prioritized, what was sacrificed, and whether the tradeoff was right. Every design decision trades something. Use when evaluating design decisions, defending choices, or helping teams understand what they're giving up.

discovered.name: type-as-signal
discovered.description: Read a designer's taste through their typography decisions alone. Type is the fastest taste signal in any design. Use when evaluating design maturity, assessing portfolio quality, or understanding what typography reveals about design thinking.

discovered.name: type-selection
discovered.description: Choose typefaces based on voice and context, not trends. Use when selecting fonts for a project, evaluating type choices, or understanding what a typeface communicates before anyone reads a word.

discovered.name: type-systems
discovered.description: Scale, weight, line height, and tracking as a coherent system. Use when building type scales, auditing typography consistency, or diagnosing why text feels off.

discovered.name: typescript-expert
discovered.description: Design, implement, refactor, or review TypeScript and TSX when correctness or maintainability depends on type models, inference, component contracts, public APIs, generics, external-data boundaries, or module/compiler settings. Use when these needs are explicit or emerge during work. Follow the target project and installed TypeScript version; skip prose, formatting, and mechanical edits without type judgment.

discovered.name: verification-before-completion
discovered.description: Verify implementations, fixes, refactors, configuration changes, and consequential task results before reporting completion or correctness. Use project tests, type checks, builds, runtime checks, or inspection in proportion to changed behavior. Reuse still-valid task evidence, rerun affected checks after changes, and report failures or unverified limits. Skip discussion and prose-only tasks without engineering claims.

discovered.name: version-archaeology
discovered.description: Study how products evolve over time using archived versions. The decisions that survive redesigns are the taste decisions. Use when understanding what's essential vs. cosmetic in a design, or learning from product evolution.

discovered.name: visual-audit
discovered.description: The 10-second design audit. Look at any design and name what's working and what's not within seconds. Trains rapid pattern recognition for hierarchy, spacing, type, and color. Use when evaluating designs quickly, giving first-impression feedback, or building perception speed.

discovered.name: written-critique
discovered.description: Write a structured design review that someone can act on without follow-up questions. Use when giving async design feedback, writing portfolio case studies, or documenting design decisions.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

tools.name: tool_search
tools.description:
# Tool discovery

Searches over deferred tool metadata with BM25 and exposes matching tools for the next model call.

Some of the tools, such as tools of MCP servers, may not have been provided to you upfront, and you should use this tool (`tool_search`) to search for the required tools. For MCP tool discovery, always use `tool_search`.

limit.description: Maximum number of tools to return. Defaults to 8.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search relevant Global and current Project knowledge. History is opt-in; unavailable sources are reported.

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description: Read one visible memory, optionally with scoped revision history and Session/Entry references.

tools.name: memory_save
tools.description: Save useful descriptive knowledge, not rules. Project decisions depend on their source branch; general experience survives rollback. Label unverified ideas hypothesis.

tools.name: memory_revise
tools.description: Append a correction or supplement with evidence and baseRevision. confirm=true explicitly establishes a new current basis, including for withdrawn knowledge.

tools.name: memory_retire
tools.description: Withdraw outdated knowledge with a reason, preserving evidence and revision history.

tools.name: diagnostic_search
tools.description: Search observed execution metrics across Sessions in the current project, including historical branches. No transcript is injected automatically.

tools.name: diagnostic_get
tools.description: Read one visible Trace, with paginated native Turn, Tool, compaction and retry metrics and precise Session/Entry references.

tools.name: diagnostic_evidence
tools.description: Read a protected, paginated native Session Entry in the current project. Existing Memory sources work without a Trace. Nested calls have bounded summaries, not full result bodies.

tools.name: suggestion_submit
tools.description: Save a capability improvement idea with evidence, expected value and uncertainty for user discussion.

discovered.name: impeccable
discovered.description: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, simplify, harden, animate, or otherwise improve a frontend interface: websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, components, forms, settings, onboarding, empty states, and native iOS or Android screens. Handles UX review, hierarchy, layout, typography, color, motion, UX copy, accessibility, responsive behavior, edge cases, and capturing or documenting design systems (DESIGN.md, tokens). Also for making bland UI bolder, loud UI quieter, or ambitious visual effects. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks.

discovered.name: absence-audit
discovered.description: Notice what's deliberately missing from a design. Restraint is a taste signal. Use when studying minimalist products, evaluating design maturity, or understanding the power of removal.

discovered.name: audience-translation
discovered.description: Explain the same design observation to a designer, a developer, and a non-technical stakeholder. Same insight, three languages. Use when working cross-functionally or presenting design decisions to mixed audiences.

discovered.name: color-systems
discovered.description: Palette roles, restraint, semantic consistency, and when fewer colors means better design. Use when building color palettes, evaluating color usage, or diagnosing color-related design problems.

discovered.name: constraint-evaluation
discovered.description: Understand the constraints a design was built under and evaluate quality within that context. Use when reviewing work that had limited time, budget, or team size, or when assessing whether constraints were handled well.

discovered.name: consumption-discipline
discovered.description: Structured exposure habits for building taste through relentless, intentional consumption. Not passive scrolling. Active intake across design, architecture, film, music, food, and culture. Use when building a taste practice, advising on professional development, or diagnosing why someone's design range feels narrow.

discovered.name: craft-signals
discovered.description: Consistent radii, pixel-perfect alignment, state coverage, and the details that signal design quality. Use when polishing designs, auditing quality, or evaluating whether a design is ready to ship.

discovered.name: critique-vocabulary
discovered.description: Precise language for design feedback. Ban vague words. Name what you actually see. Use when giving design feedback, running critiques, or training teams to communicate about quality.

discovered.name: cross-domain-seeing
discovered.description: Pull design principles from architecture, fashion, film, industrial design, and physical spaces into screen-based design. Use when seeking inspiration beyond digital, expanding creative range, or building cross-disciplinary design vocabulary.

discovered.name: cross-pollination
discovered.description: Draw from architecture, fashion, music, food, and industrial design to expand your design taste range. Use when seeking inspiration beyond digital, building diverse reference sets, or expanding creative vocabulary.

discovered.name: daily-routines
discovered.description: 15-minute daily taste exercises. Monday through Friday. Compound effect over time. Use when building personal practice habits, training a team's design eye, or adding structure to professional development.

discovered.name: decision-tracing
discovered.description: Reverse-engineer why a design decision was made. Move from observation to inference. Use when studying products you admire, learning from competitors, or building analytical design thinking.

discovered.name: design-critique
discovered.description: Run taste-informed design reviews using Observation > Principle > Question. Use when facilitating design critiques, improving feedback quality on a team, or building a shared vocabulary for quality.

discovered.name: design-ranking
discovered.description: Rank multiple design solutions and explain why. Separate personal preference from quality judgment. Use when comparing design options, evaluating competing approaches, or making design decisions with clear reasoning.

discovered.name: design-rationale
discovered.description: Defend a design decision to skeptical stakeholders with structure and evidence. Use when presenting design work, writing design documentation, or pushing back on requests to change something.

discovered.name: detail-observation
discovered.description: Micro-decision analysis. Catalog the border radii, spacing scales, type sizes, and state coverage that most people miss. Use when auditing design systems, evaluating craft quality, or training granular perception.

discovered.name: dg-piagent
discovered.description:
Use when working with pi-agent / @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent SDK — 创建 agent、自定义工具、
编写扩展、修改系统提示词、管理会话、配置模型、处理认证、加载 skills/prompts/context files、
实现完全控制模式、或任何需要调用 pi-agent SDK API 的任务时使用。
也用于企业内网接口接入评估：用户给出企业/内网 LLM 接口文档或地址，问「能不能接」「怎么配」时，
按接口核对清单给出接入建议 + models.json 配置初稿。
触发关键词：createAgentSession、AgentSession、pi.on、session.subscribe、extensionFactories、
ModelRegistry、defineTool、pi-coding-agent、pi-ai、@earendil-works、SSE 流式集成、
企业接口文档、内网模型接入、OpenAI 兼容判断、接口接入评估。

discovered.name: field-notes
discovered.description: Structured taste breakdowns of real products. The format for making taste observations legible and shareable. Use when analyzing products, writing case studies, documenting design observations, or teaching through example.

discovered.name: flow-patterns
discovered.description: Task sequences, progressive disclosure, and the pacing of an experience over time. Use when designing multi-step flows, evaluating onboarding, or diagnosing why users get lost.

discovered.name: hierarchy-principles
discovered.description: Visual weight, attention order, and the decisions that guide the eye. Use when building layouts, evaluating information architecture, or diagnosing why a design feels confusing.

discovered.name: learning-by-making
discovered.description: Build taste through volume of output, deliberate failure, and speed. Taste cannot be developed by watching. It's sharpened by making, failing, and making again. Use when designing practice routines, breaking through creative blocks, or helping someone move from analysis to execution.

discovered.name: library-architecture
discovered.description: Build a reference system that returns the right reference in under 60 seconds. Use when setting up a design reference library, reorganizing existing collections, or helping teams build shared reference systems.

discovered.name: motion-design
discovered.description: Animation as communication. Feedback, orientation, emphasis, delight. If motion doesn't serve one of these four purposes, it shouldn't exist. Use when evaluating animation quality, designing transitions, or deciding whether motion adds or subtracts.

discovered.name: principle-tagging
discovered.description: Tag design references by principle, not aesthetic. Build a library you can actually search. Use when saving references, organizing inspiration, or building a design library that returns useful results.

discovered.name: python-anti-patterns
discovered.description: Diagnose and review Python problems in exception handling, repeated infrastructure logic, resource lifetime, async blocking, input and type contracts, or harmful coupling. Use during debugging, review, legacy maintenance, or implementation when concrete risks appear. Judge behavior and maintenance cost before changing code; skip unrelated or mechanical edits and harmless intentional duplication.

discovered.name: python-design-patterns
discovered.description: Guide Python feature design, implementation, and refactoring when responsibilities, coupling, module boundaries, testability, or extensibility require structural judgment. Use for tangled services, entangled I/O, or meaningful abstraction choices, including problems discovered during work. Choose the simplest maintainable design supported by the project; skip mechanical edits with no design decision.

discovered.name: quality-checklist
discovered.description: Systematic design quality evaluation. Hierarchy, type, color, space, craft, system. Use when evaluating whether a design is ready to ship, running quality audits, or setting quality standards.

discovered.name: screenshot-surgery
discovered.description: Annotate and map the anatomy of any design. Identify visual hierarchy, spacing systems, color roles, and tension points through clinical analysis. Use when doing formal design audits, teaching design analysis, or building structured observation skills.

discovered.name: search-first
discovered.description: Discover reusable repository code, dependencies, libraries, and extension points when adding or changing features, integrations, shared components, or utilities. Use when reuse could affect an implementation choice, including implicit needs discovered during work. Start with the project; research externally only to resolve a concrete gap. Skip prose and mechanical edits without such choices.

discovered.name: self-assessment
discovered.description: Diagnose your taste gaps across six skill areas. Know what to practice. Use when starting a taste development program, checking progress, or identifying specific areas to improve.

discovered.name: spatial-rhythm
discovered.description: Density, whitespace, rhythm, and how space communicates relationships between elements. Use when building layouts, evaluating spacing consistency, or diagnosing why a design feels cramped or empty.

discovered.name: system-deconstruction
discovered.description: Break a design system into its constituent decisions and evaluate each one. Use when auditing design systems, evaluating consistency, or understanding how a product maintains quality at scale.

discovered.name: taste-as-strategy
discovered.description: Use taste as a competitive moat and business advantage. In the AI and vibe-coding era, execution is commoditized. Taste is the defensible edge. Use when advising founders on product differentiation, building product culture, evaluating why some products win despite fewer features, or understanding taste as a strategic asset.

discovered.name: taste-gap
discovered.description: Navigate the gap between what you can see and what you can make. The Ira Glass gap. Use when a designer is frustrated by the distance between their taste and their output, when mentoring someone through a creative plateau, or when someone is considering quitting because their work doesn't match their vision.

discovered.name: taste-vs-trends
discovered.description: Tell the difference between design decisions that age well and decisions that follow the crowd. Use when evaluating whether a design choice is principled or fashionable, or when a client asks to 'make it look modern.'

discovered.name: teaching-taste
discovered.description: Help other designers develop judgment without imposing your style. Use when mentoring designers, running design education, or building team-wide quality standards.

discovered.name: timing-feedback
discovered.description: Response timing, acknowledgment, and making the interface feel alive. Every action deserves a response at the right speed. Use when designing interactions, evaluating responsiveness, or diagnosing why a product feels sluggish or dead.

discovered.name: tradeoff-assessment
discovered.description: Name what was prioritized, what was sacrificed, and whether the tradeoff was right. Every design decision trades something. Use when evaluating design decisions, defending choices, or helping teams understand what they're giving up.

discovered.name: type-as-signal
discovered.description: Read a designer's taste through their typography decisions alone. Type is the fastest taste signal in any design. Use when evaluating design maturity, assessing portfolio quality, or understanding what typography reveals about design thinking.

discovered.name: type-selection
discovered.description: Choose typefaces based on voice and context, not trends. Use when selecting fonts for a project, evaluating type choices, or understanding what a typeface communicates before anyone reads a word.

discovered.name: type-systems
discovered.description: Scale, weight, line height, and tracking as a coherent system. Use when building type scales, auditing typography consistency, or diagnosing why text feels off.

discovered.name: typescript-expert
discovered.description: Design, implement, refactor, or review TypeScript and TSX when correctness or maintainability depends on type models, inference, component contracts, public APIs, generics, external-data boundaries, or module/compiler settings. Use when these needs are explicit or emerge during work. Follow the target project and installed TypeScript version; skip prose, formatting, and mechanical edits without type judgment.

discovered.name: verification-before-completion
discovered.description: Verify implementations, fixes, refactors, configuration changes, and consequential task results before reporting completion or correctness. Use project tests, type checks, builds, runtime checks, or inspection in proportion to changed behavior. Reuse still-valid task evidence, rerun affected checks after changes, and report failures or unverified limits. Skip discussion and prose-only tasks without engineering claims.

discovered.name: version-archaeology
discovered.description: Study how products evolve over time using archived versions. The decisions that survive redesigns are the taste decisions. Use when understanding what's essential vs. cosmetic in a design, or learning from product evolution.

discovered.name: visual-audit
discovered.description: The 10-second design audit. Look at any design and name what's working and what's not within seconds. Trains rapid pattern recognition for hierarchy, spacing, type, and color. Use when evaluating designs quickly, giving first-impression feedback, or building perception speed.

discovered.name: written-critique
discovered.description: Write a structured design review that someone can act on without follow-up questions. Use when giving async design feedback, writing portfolio case studies, or documenting design decisions.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

pattern.description: Search pattern (regex or literal string)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of results (default: 1000)

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

path.description: Directory to list (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

tools.name: powershell
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: tool_search
tools.description:
# Tool discovery

Searches over deferred tool metadata with BM25 and exposes matching tools for the next model call.

Some of the tools, such as tools of MCP servers, may not have been provided to you upfront, and you should use this tool (`tool_search`) to search for the required tools. For MCP tool discovery, always use `tool_search`.

limit.description: Maximum number of tools to return. Defaults to 8.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search relevant Global and current Project knowledge. History is opt-in; unavailable sources are reported.

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description: Read one visible memory, optionally with scoped revision history and Session/Entry references.

tools.name: memory_save
tools.description: Save useful descriptive knowledge, not rules. Project decisions depend on their source branch; general experience survives rollback. Label unverified ideas hypothesis.

tools.name: memory_revise
tools.description: Append a correction or supplement with evidence and baseRevision. confirm=true explicitly establishes a new current basis, including for withdrawn knowledge.

tools.name: memory_retire
tools.description: Withdraw outdated knowledge with a reason, preserving evidence and revision history.

tools.name: diagnostic_search
tools.description: Search observed execution metrics across Sessions in the current project, including historical branches. No transcript is injected automatically.

tools.name: diagnostic_get
tools.description: Read one visible Trace, with paginated native Turn, Tool, compaction and retry metrics and precise Session/Entry references.

tools.name: diagnostic_evidence
tools.description: Read a protected, paginated native Session Entry in the current project. Existing Memory sources work without a Trace. Nested calls have bounded summaries, not full result bodies.

tools.name: suggestion_submit
tools.description: Save a capability improvement idea with evidence, expected value and uncertainty for user discussion.

discovered.description: Draw from architecture, fashion, music, food, and industrial design to expand your design taste range. Use when seeking inspiration beyond digital, building diverse reference sets, or expanding creative vocabulary.

discovered.name: daily-routines
discovered.description: 15-minute daily taste exercises. Monday through Friday. Compound effect over time. Use when building personal practice habits, training a team's design eye, or adding structure to professional development.

discovered.name: decision-tracing
discovered.description: Reverse-engineer why a design decision was made. Move from observation to inference. Use when studying products you admire, learning from competitors, or building analytical design thinking.

discovered.name: design-critique
discovered.description: Run taste-informed design reviews using Observation > Principle > Question. Use when facilitating design critiques, improving feedback quality on a team, or building a shared vocabulary for quality.

discovered.name: design-ranking
discovered.description: Rank multiple design solutions and explain why. Separate personal preference from quality judgment. Use when comparing design options, evaluating competing approaches, or making design decisions with clear reasoning.

discovered.name: design-rationale
discovered.description: Defend a design decision to skeptical stakeholders with structure and evidence. Use when presenting design work, writing design documentation, or pushing back on requests to change something.

discovered.name: detail-observation
discovered.description: Micro-decision analysis. Catalog the border radii, spacing scales, type sizes, and state coverage that most people miss. Use when auditing design systems, evaluating craft quality, or training granular perception.

discovered.name: dg-piagent
discovered.description:
Use when working with pi-agent / @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent SDK — 创建 agent、自定义工具、
编写扩展、修改系统提示词、管理会话、配置模型、处理认证、加载 skills/prompts/context files、
实现完全控制模式、或任何需要调用 pi-agent SDK API 的任务时使用。
也用于企业内网接口接入评估：用户给出企业/内网 LLM 接口文档或地址，问「能不能接」「怎么配」时，
按接口核对清单给出接入建议 + models.json 配置初稿。
触发关键词：createAgentSession、AgentSession、pi.on、session.subscribe、extensionFactories、
ModelRegistry、defineTool、pi-coding-agent、pi-ai、@earendil-works、SSE 流式集成、
企业接口文档、内网模型接入、OpenAI 兼容判断、接口接入评估。

discovered.name: field-notes
discovered.description: Structured taste breakdowns of real products. The format for making taste observations legible and shareable. Use when analyzing products, writing case studies, documenting design observations, or teaching through example.

discovered.name: flow-patterns
discovered.description: Task sequences, progressive disclosure, and the pacing of an experience over time. Use when designing multi-step flows, evaluating onboarding, or diagnosing why users get lost.

discovered.name: hierarchy-principles
discovered.description: Visual weight, attention order, and the decisions that guide the eye. Use when building layouts, evaluating information architecture, or diagnosing why a design feels confusing.

discovered.name: learning-by-making
discovered.description: Build taste through volume of output, deliberate failure, and speed. Taste cannot be developed by watching. It's sharpened by making, failing, and making again. Use when designing practice routines, breaking through creative blocks, or helping someone move from analysis to execution.

discovered.name: library-architecture
discovered.description: Build a reference system that returns the right reference in under 60 seconds. Use when setting up a design reference library, reorganizing existing collections, or helping teams build shared reference systems.

discovered.name: motion-design
discovered.description: Animation as communication. Feedback, orientation, emphasis, delight. If motion doesn't serve one of these four purposes, it shouldn't exist. Use when evaluating animation quality, designing transitions, or deciding whether motion adds or subtracts.

discovered.name: principle-tagging
discovered.description: Tag design references by principle, not aesthetic. Build a library you can actually search. Use when saving references, organizing inspiration, or building a design library that returns useful results.

discovered.name: python-anti-patterns
discovered.description: Diagnose and review Python problems in exception handling, repeated infrastructure logic, resource lifetime, async blocking, input and type contracts, or harmful coupling. Use during debugging, review, legacy maintenance, or implementation when concrete risks appear. Judge behavior and maintenance cost before changing code; skip unrelated or mechanical edits and harmless intentional duplication.

discovered.name: python-design-patterns
discovered.description: Guide Python feature design, implementation, and refactoring when responsibilities, coupling, module boundaries, testability, or extensibility require structural judgment. Use for tangled services, entangled I/O, or meaningful abstraction choices, including problems discovered during work. Choose the simplest maintainable design supported by the project; skip mechanical edits with no design decision.

discovered.name: quality-checklist
discovered.description: Systematic design quality evaluation. Hierarchy, type, color, space, craft, system. Use when evaluating whether a design is ready to ship, running quality audits, or setting quality standards.

discovered.name: screenshot-surgery
discovered.description: Annotate and map the anatomy of any design. Identify visual hierarchy, spacing systems, color roles, and tension points through clinical analysis. Use when doing formal design audits, teaching design analysis, or building structured observation skills.

discovered.name: search-first
discovered.description: Discover reusable repository code, dependencies, libraries, and extension points when adding or changing features, integrations, shared components, or utilities. Use when reuse could affect an implementation choice, including implicit needs discovered during work. Start with the project; research externally only to resolve a concrete gap. Skip prose and mechanical edits without such choices.

discovered.name: self-assessment
discovered.description: Diagnose your taste gaps across six skill areas. Know what to practice. Use when starting a taste development program, checking progress, or identifying specific areas to improve.

discovered.name: spatial-rhythm
discovered.description: Density, whitespace, rhythm, and how space communicates relationships between elements. Use when building layouts, evaluating spacing consistency, or diagnosing why a design feels cramped or empty.

discovered.name: system-deconstruction
discovered.description: Break a design system into its constituent decisions and evaluate each one. Use when auditing design systems, evaluating consistency, or understanding how a product maintains quality at scale.

discovered.name: taste-as-strategy
discovered.description: Use taste as a competitive moat and business advantage. In the AI and vibe-coding era, execution is commoditized. Taste is the defensible edge. Use when advising founders on product differentiation, building product culture, evaluating why some products win despite fewer features, or understanding taste as a strategic asset.

discovered.name: taste-gap
discovered.description: Navigate the gap between what you can see and what you can make. The Ira Glass gap. Use when a designer is frustrated by the distance between their taste and their output, when mentoring someone through a creative plateau, or when someone is considering quitting because their work doesn't match their vision.

discovered.name: taste-vs-trends
discovered.description: Tell the difference between design decisions that age well and decisions that follow the crowd. Use when evaluating whether a design choice is principled or fashionable, or when a client asks to 'make it look modern.'

discovered.name: teaching-taste
discovered.description: Help other designers develop judgment without imposing your style. Use when mentoring designers, running design education, or building team-wide quality standards.

discovered.name: timing-feedback
discovered.description: Response timing, acknowledgment, and making the interface feel alive. Every action deserves a response at the right speed. Use when designing interactions, evaluating responsiveness, or diagnosing why a product feels sluggish or dead.

discovered.name: tradeoff-assessment
discovered.description: Name what was prioritized, what was sacrificed, and whether the tradeoff was right. Every design decision trades something. Use when evaluating design decisions, defending choices, or helping teams understand what they're giving up.

discovered.name: type-as-signal
discovered.description: Read a designer's taste through their typography decisions alone. Type is the fastest taste signal in any design. Use when evaluating design maturity, assessing portfolio quality, or understanding what typography reveals about design thinking.

discovered.name: type-selection
discovered.description: Choose typefaces based on voice and context, not trends. Use when selecting fonts for a project, evaluating type choices, or understanding what a typeface communicates before anyone reads a word.

discovered.name: type-systems
discovered.description: Scale, weight, line height, and tracking as a coherent system. Use when building type scales, auditing typography consistency, or diagnosing why text feels off.

discovered.name: typescript-expert
discovered.description: Design, implement, refactor, or review TypeScript and TSX when correctness or maintainability depends on type models, inference, component contracts, public APIs, generics, external-data boundaries, or module/compiler settings. Use when these needs are explicit or emerge during work. Follow the target project and installed TypeScript version; skip prose, formatting, and mechanical edits without type judgment.

discovered.name: verification-before-completion
discovered.description: Verify implementations, fixes, refactors, configuration changes, and consequential task results before reporting completion or correctness. Use project tests, type checks, builds, runtime checks, or inspection in proportion to changed behavior. Reuse still-valid task evidence, rerun affected checks after changes, and report failures or unverified limits. Skip discussion and prose-only tasks without engineering claims.

discovered.name: version-archaeology
discovered.description: Study how products evolve over time using archived versions. The decisions that survive redesigns are the taste decisions. Use when understanding what's essential vs. cosmetic in a design, or learning from product evolution.

discovered.name: visual-audit
discovered.description: The 10-second design audit. Look at any design and name what's working and what's not within seconds. Trains rapid pattern recognition for hierarchy, spacing, type, and color. Use when evaluating designs quickly, giving first-impression feedback, or building perception speed.

discovered.name: written-critique
discovered.description: Write a structured design review that someone can act on without follow-up questions. Use when giving async design feedback, writing portfolio case studies, or documenting design decisions.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

pattern.description: Search pattern (regex or literal string)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of results (default: 1000)

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

path.description: Directory to list (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

discovered.name: impeccable
discovered.description: Use when the user wants to design, redesign, shape, critique, audit, polish, simplify, harden, animate, or otherwise improve a frontend interface: websites, landing pages, dashboards, product UI, components, forms, settings, onboarding, empty states, and native iOS or Android screens. Handles UX review, hierarchy, layout, typography, color, motion, UX copy, accessibility, responsive behavior, edge cases, and capturing or documenting design systems (DESIGN.md, tokens). Also for making bland UI bolder, loud UI quieter, or ambitious visual effects. Not for backend-only or non-UI tasks.

discovered.name: absence-audit
discovered.description: Notice what's deliberately missing from a design. Restraint is a taste signal. Use when studying minimalist products, evaluating design maturity, or understanding the power of removal.

discovered.name: audience-translation
discovered.description: Explain the same design observation to a designer, a developer, and a non-technical stakeholder. Same insight, three languages. Use when working cross-functionally or presenting design decisions to mixed audiences.

discovered.name: color-systems
discovered.description: Palette roles, restraint, semantic consistency, and when fewer colors means better design. Use when building color palettes, evaluating color usage, or diagnosing color-related design problems.

discovered.name: constraint-evaluation
discovered.description: Understand the constraints a design was built under and evaluate quality within that context. Use when reviewing work that had limited time, budget, or team size, or when assessing whether constraints were handled well.

discovered.name: consumption-discipline
discovered.description: Structured exposure habits for building taste through relentless, intentional consumption. Not passive scrolling. Active intake across design, architecture, film, music, food, and culture. Use when building a taste practice, advising on professional development, or diagnosing why someone's design range feels narrow.

discovered.name: craft-signals
discovered.description: Consistent radii, pixel-perfect alignment, state coverage, and the details that signal design quality. Use when polishing designs, auditing quality, or evaluating whether a design is ready to ship.

discovered.name: critique-vocabulary
discovered.description: Precise language for design feedback. Ban vague words. Name what you actually see. Use when giving design feedback, running critiques, or training teams to communicate about quality.

discovered.name: cross-domain-seeing
discovered.description: Pull design principles from architecture, fashion, film, industrial design, and physical spaces into screen-based design. Use when seeking inspiration beyond digital, expanding creative range, or building cross-disciplinary design vocabulary.

discovered.name: cross-pollination
discovered.description: Draw from architecture, fashion, music, food, and industrial design to expand your design taste range. Use when seeking inspiration beyond digital, building diverse reference sets, or expanding creative vocabulary.

discovered.name: daily-routines
discovered.description: 15-minute daily taste exercises. Monday through Friday. Compound effect over time. Use when building personal practice habits, training a team's design eye, or adding structure to professional development.

discovered.name: decision-tracing
discovered.description: Reverse-engineer why a design decision was made. Move from observation to inference. Use when studying products you admire, learning from competitors, or building analytical design thinking.

discovered.name: design-critique
discovered.description: Run taste-informed design reviews using Observation > Principle > Question. Use when facilitating design critiques, improving feedback quality on a team, or building a shared vocabulary for quality.

discovered.name: design-ranking
discovered.description: Rank multiple design solutions and explain why. Separate personal preference from quality judgment. Use when comparing design options, evaluating competing approaches, or making design decisions with clear reasoning.

discovered.name: design-rationale
discovered.description: Defend a design decision to skeptical stakeholders with structure and evidence. Use when presenting design work, writing design documentation, or pushing back on requests to change something.

discovered.name: detail-observation
discovered.description: Micro-decision analysis. Catalog the border radii, spacing scales, type sizes, and state coverage that most people miss. Use when auditing design systems, evaluating craft quality, or training granular perception.

discovered.name: dg-piagent
discovered.description:
Use when working with pi-agent / @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent SDK — 创建 agent、自定义工具、
编写扩展、修改系统提示词、管理会话、配置模型、处理认证、加载 skills/prompts/context files、
实现完全控制模式、或任何需要调用 pi-agent SDK API 的任务时使用。
也用于企业内网接口接入评估：用户给出企业/内网 LLM 接口文档或地址，问「能不能接」「怎么配」时，
按接口核对清单给出接入建议 + models.json 配置初稿。
触发关键词：createAgentSession、AgentSession、pi.on、session.subscribe、extensionFactories、
ModelRegistry、defineTool、pi-coding-agent、pi-ai、@earendil-works、SSE 流式集成、
企业接口文档、内网模型接入、OpenAI 兼容判断、接口接入评估。

discovered.name: field-notes
discovered.description: Structured taste breakdowns of real products. The format for making taste observations legible and shareable. Use when analyzing products, writing case studies, documenting design observations, or teaching through example.

discovered.name: flow-patterns
discovered.description: Task sequences, progressive disclosure, and the pacing of an experience over time. Use when designing multi-step flows, evaluating onboarding, or diagnosing why users get lost.

discovered.name: hierarchy-principles
discovered.description: Visual weight, attention order, and the decisions that guide the eye. Use when building layouts, evaluating information architecture, or diagnosing why a design feels confusing.

discovered.name: learning-by-making
discovered.description: Build taste through volume of output, deliberate failure, and speed. Taste cannot be developed by watching. It's sharpened by making, failing, and making again. Use when designing practice routines, breaking through creative blocks, or helping someone move from analysis to execution.

discovered.name: library-architecture
discovered.description: Build a reference system that returns the right reference in under 60 seconds. Use when setting up a design reference library, reorganizing existing collections, or helping teams build shared reference systems.

discovered.name: motion-design
discovered.description: Animation as communication. Feedback, orientation, emphasis, delight. If motion doesn't serve one of these four purposes, it shouldn't exist. Use when evaluating animation quality, designing transitions, or deciding whether motion adds or subtracts.

discovered.name: principle-tagging
discovered.description: Tag design references by principle, not aesthetic. Build a library you can actually search. Use when saving references, organizing inspiration, or building a design library that returns useful results.

discovered.name: python-anti-patterns
discovered.description: Diagnose and review Python problems in exception handling, repeated infrastructure logic, resource lifetime, async blocking, input and type contracts, or harmful coupling. Use during debugging, review, legacy maintenance, or implementation when concrete risks appear. Judge behavior and maintenance cost before changing code; skip unrelated or mechanical edits and harmless intentional duplication.

discovered.name: python-design-patterns
discovered.description: Guide Python feature design, implementation, and refactoring when responsibilities, coupling, module boundaries, testability, or extensibility require structural judgment. Use for tangled services, entangled I/O, or meaningful abstraction choices, including problems discovered during work. Choose the simplest maintainable design supported by the project; skip mechanical edits with no design decision.

discovered.name: quality-checklist
discovered.description: Systematic design quality evaluation. Hierarchy, type, color, space, craft, system. Use when evaluating whether a design is ready to ship, running quality audits, or setting quality standards.

discovered.name: screenshot-surgery
discovered.description: Annotate and map the anatomy of any design. Identify visual hierarchy, spacing systems, color roles, and tension points through clinical analysis. Use when doing formal design audits, teaching design analysis, or building structured observation skills.

discovered.name: search-first
discovered.description: Discover reusable repository code, dependencies, libraries, and extension points when adding or changing features, integrations, shared components, or utilities. Use when reuse could affect an implementation choice, including implicit needs discovered during work. Start with the project; research externally only to resolve a concrete gap. Skip prose and mechanical edits without such choices.

discovered.name: self-assessment
discovered.description: Diagnose your taste gaps across six skill areas. Know what to practice. Use when starting a taste development program, checking progress, or identifying specific areas to improve.

discovered.name: spatial-rhythm
discovered.description: Density, whitespace, rhythm, and how space communicates relationships between elements. Use when building layouts, evaluating spacing consistency, or diagnosing why a design feels cramped or empty.

discovered.name: system-deconstruction
discovered.description: Break a design system into its constituent decisions and evaluate each one. Use when auditing design systems, evaluating consistency, or understanding how a product maintains quality at scale.

discovered.name: taste-as-strategy
discovered.description: Use taste as a competitive moat and business advantage. In the AI and vibe-coding era, execution is commoditized. Taste is the defensible edge. Use when advising founders on product differentiation, building product culture, evaluating why some products win despite fewer features, or understanding taste as a strategic asset.

discovered.name: taste-gap
discovered.description: Navigate the gap between what you can see and what you can make. The Ira Glass gap. Use when a designer is frustrated by the distance between their taste and their output, when mentoring someone through a creative plateau, or when someone is considering quitting because their work doesn't match their vision.

discovered.name: taste-vs-trends
discovered.description: Tell the difference between design decisions that age well and decisions that follow the crowd. Use when evaluating whether a design choice is principled or fashionable, or when a client asks to 'make it look modern.'

discovered.name: teaching-taste
discovered.description: Help other designers develop judgment without imposing your style. Use when mentoring designers, running design education, or building team-wide quality standards.

discovered.name: timing-feedback
discovered.description: Response timing, acknowledgment, and making the interface feel alive. Every action deserves a response at the right speed. Use when designing interactions, evaluating responsiveness, or diagnosing why a product feels sluggish or dead.

discovered.name: tradeoff-assessment
discovered.description: Name what was prioritized, what was sacrificed, and whether the tradeoff was right. Every design decision trades something. Use when evaluating design decisions, defending choices, or helping teams understand what they're giving up.

discovered.name: type-as-signal
discovered.description: Read a designer's taste through their typography decisions alone. Type is the fastest taste signal in any design. Use when evaluating design maturity, assessing portfolio quality, or understanding what typography reveals about design thinking.

discovered.name: type-selection
discovered.description: Choose typefaces based on voice and context, not trends. Use when selecting fonts for a project, evaluating type choices, or understanding what a typeface communicates before anyone reads a word.

discovered.name: type-systems
discovered.description: Scale, weight, line height, and tracking as a coherent system. Use when building type scales, auditing typography consistency, or diagnosing why text feels off.

discovered.name: typescript-expert
discovered.description: Design, implement, refactor, or review TypeScript and TSX when correctness or maintainability depends on type models, inference, component contracts, public APIs, generics, external-data boundaries, or module/compiler settings. Use when these needs are explicit or emerge during work. Follow the target project and installed TypeScript version; skip prose, formatting, and mechanical edits without type judgment.

discovered.name: verification-before-completion
discovered.description: Verify implementations, fixes, refactors, configuration changes, and consequential task results before reporting completion or correctness. Use project tests, type checks, builds, runtime checks, or inspection in proportion to changed behavior. Reuse still-valid task evidence, rerun affected checks after changes, and report failures or unverified limits. Skip discussion and prose-only tasks without engineering claims.

discovered.name: version-archaeology
discovered.description: Study how products evolve over time using archived versions. The decisions that survive redesigns are the taste decisions. Use when understanding what's essential vs. cosmetic in a design, or learning from product evolution.

discovered.name: visual-audit
discovered.description: The 10-second design audit. Look at any design and name what's working and what's not within seconds. Trains rapid pattern recognition for hierarchy, spacing, type, and color. Use when evaluating designs quickly, giving first-impression feedback, or building perception speed.

discovered.name: written-critique
discovered.description: Write a structured design review that someone can act on without follow-up questions. Use when giving async design feedback, writing portfolio case studies, or documenting design decisions.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

pattern.description: Search pattern (regex or literal string)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of results (default: 1000)

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

path.description: Directory to list (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: tool_search
tools.description:
# Tool discovery

Searches over deferred tool metadata with BM25 and exposes matching tools for the next model call.

Some of the tools, such as tools of MCP servers, may not have been provided to you upfront, and you should use this tool (`tool_search`) to search for the required tools. For MCP tool discovery, always use `tool_search`.

limit.description: Maximum number of tools to return. Defaults to 8.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Search relevant Global and current Project knowledge. History is opt-in; unavailable sources are reported.

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description: Read one visible memory, optionally with scoped revision history and Session/Entry references.

tools.name: memory_save
tools.description: Save useful descriptive knowledge, not rules. Project decisions depend on their source branch; general experience survives rollback. Label unverified ideas hypothesis.

tools.name: memory_revise
tools.description: Append a correction or supplement with evidence and baseRevision. confirm=true explicitly establishes a new current basis, including for withdrawn knowledge.

tools.name: memory_retire
tools.description: Withdraw outdated knowledge with a reason, preserving evidence and revision history.

tools.name: diagnostic_search
tools.description: Search observed execution metrics across Sessions in the current project, including historical branches. No transcript is injected automatically.

tools.name: diagnostic_get
tools.description: Read one visible Trace, with paginated native Turn, Tool, compaction and retry metrics and precise Session/Entry references.

tools.name: diagnostic_evidence
tools.description: Read a protected, paginated native Session Entry in the current project. Existing Memory sources work without a Trace. Nested calls have bounded summaries, not full result bodies.

tools.name: suggestion_submit
tools.description: Save a capability improvement idea with evidence, expected value and uncertainty for user discussion.
